front_blocks.md: Define the **system life cycle**.

cards.front_md: Define the **system life cycle**.

front_blocks.md: What is the purpose of the analysis stage?

back_blocks.md: The purpose of the analysis stage is to gather detailed **requirements** from stakeholders and analyse them to understand **what the system should accomplish**.

cards.front_md: What is the purpose of the analysis stage?
cards.back_md: The purpose of the analysis stage is to gather detailed **requirements** from stakeholders and analyse them to understand **what the system should accomplish**.

front_blocks.md: Name the four research methods a systems analyst can use.

back_blocks.md: The four research methods are **observation**, **questionnaires**, **interviews** and **looking at the existing system**, including its paperwork.

cards.front_md: Name the four research methods a systems analyst can use.
cards.back_md: The four research methods are **observation**, **questionnaires**, **interviews** and **looking at the existing system**, including its paperwork.

front_blocks.md: Define **observation** as a research method.

back_blocks.md: Observation is watching users **interact with the current system** to see how it acts and works.

cards.front_md: Define **observation** as a research method.
cards.back_md: Observation is watching users **interact with the current system** to see how it acts and works.

front_blocks.md: Give one disadvantage of observation.

back_blocks.md: People **do not always behave in the same way** when they are under observation.

cards.front_md: Give one disadvantage of observation.
cards.back_md: People **do not always behave in the same way** when they are under observation.

front_blocks.md: Which research method allows the analyst to change questions based on the answers given?

back_blocks.md: **Interviews** allow the analyst to change questions based on responses, because they are one-to-one question and answer sessions.

cards.front_md: Which research method allows the analyst to change questions based on the answers given?
cards.back_md: **Interviews** allow the analyst to change questions based on responses, because they are one-to-one question and answer sessions.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Interviews allow employees to remain anonymous.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Questionnaires are quick and inexpensive to use.

front_blocks.md: Give one advantage of looking at the existing system.

back_blocks.md: Looking at the existing system lets the analyst **obtain information that cannot be obtained from other methods**.

cards.front_md: Give one advantage of looking at the existing system.

cards.front_md: Which six key aspects must be identified when analysing the current system?

cards.front_md: Define **user requirements**.

cards.front_md: What are data flow diagrams (DFDs) used for?

front_blocks.md: What is the purpose of the design stage?

back_blocks.md: The purpose of the design stage is to develop architectural **blueprints for the system**, including **database design**, **user interfaces** and **system interfaces**.

cards.front_md: What is the purpose of the design stage?
cards.back_md: The purpose of the design stage is to develop architectural **blueprints for the system**, including **database design**, **user interfaces** and **system interfaces**.

front_blocks.md: What four things are defined when designing a file structure?

back_blocks.md: A file structure defines **field names**, **field lengths**, **data types** and **primary keys**.

cards.front_md: What four things are defined when designing a file structure?
cards.back_md: A file structure defines **field names**, **field lengths**, **data types** and **primary keys**.

front_blocks.md: What is a file made up of?

back_blocks.md: A file consists of **records**, and records are made up of **fields**.

cards.front_md: What is a file made up of?
cards.back_md: A file consists of **records**, and records are made up of **fields**.

front_blocks.md: Define **primary key**.

back_blocks.md: A primary key is the field that **uniquely identifies each record**.

cards.front_md: Define **primary key**.
cards.back_md: A primary key is the field that **uniquely identifies each record**.

front_blocks.md: Which data type stores data in a Yes/No or True/False format?

back_blocks.md: The **Boolean** data type stores data in a Yes/No or True/False format.

cards.front_md: Which data type stores data in a Yes/No or True/False format?
cards.back_md: The **Boolean** data type stores data in a Yes/No or True/False format.

back_blocks.md: The **alphanumeric** data type would be used, because it stores a combination of **characters and numeric data**.

cards.front_md: Which data type would be used for a postcode or a product code?
cards.back_md: The **alphanumeric** data type would be used, because it stores a combination of **characters and numeric data**.

The character data type stores a single letter or symbol.

**True or False?**

The character data type stores a single letter or symbol.

**True.**

The **character** data type stores a **single letter or symbol**, such as A, B or C.

front_blocks.md: Define **validation routine**.

back_blocks.md: A validation routine is a **check placed on data being entered** to ensure it matches the design of the system.

cards.front_md: Define **validation routine**.
cards.back_md: A validation routine is a **check placed on data being entered** to ensure it matches the design of the system.

front_blocks.md: Name the six validation routines.

back_blocks.md: The six validation routines are the **range check**, **length check**, **type check**, **format check**, **presence check** and **check digit**.

cards.front_md: Name the six validation routines.
cards.back_md: The six validation routines are the **range check**, **length check**, **type check**, **format check**, **presence check** and **check digit**.

front_blocks.md: Which validation routine checks that a field has not been left blank?

back_blocks.md: A **presence check** looks to see if any data has been entered in a field.

cards.front_md: Which validation routine checks that a field has not been left blank?
cards.back_md: A **presence check** looks to see if any data has been entered in a field.

front_blocks.md: Which validation routine would check a date of birth is entered as DD/MM/YY?

back_blocks.md: A **format check** ensures that data has been entered in the **correct format**.

cards.front_md: Which validation routine would check a date of birth is entered as DD/MM/YY?
cards.back_md: A **format check** ensures that data has been entered in the **correct format**.

front_blocks.md: Define **check digit**.

back_blocks.md: A check digit is a **numerical value** that is the **final digit of a larger code**, such as a barcode.

cards.front_md: Define **check digit**.
cards.back_md: A check digit is a **numerical value** that is the **final digit of a larger code**, such as a barcode.

front_blocks.md: What is a data capture form used for?

back_blocks.md: A data capture form is used to **collect data from a user in a structured format**.

cards.front_md: What is a data capture form used for?
cards.back_md: A data capture form is used to **collect data from a user in a structured format**.

front_blocks.md: Give two ways a data capture form should aid the collection of data.

back_blocks.md: A data capture form should have a **user-friendly layout**, provide **clear instructions**, use **appropriate question types** and use **validation routines**.

cards.front_md: Give two ways a data capture form should aid the collection of data.
cards.back_md: A data capture form should have a **user-friendly layout**, provide **clear instructions**, use **appropriate question types** and use **validation routines**.

front_blocks.md: What is the purpose of the testing stage?

back_blocks.md: The purpose of testing is to verify that the system **meets all requirements**, **functions correctly** and is **free of bugs**.

cards.front_md: What is the purpose of the testing stage?
cards.back_md: The purpose of testing is to verify that the system **meets all requirements**, **functions correctly** and is **free of bugs**.

front_blocks.md: Define **test strategy**.

back_blocks.md: A test strategy is a **method of testing a completed system** to ensure **all parts work as intended**.

cards.front_md: Define **test strategy**.
cards.back_md: A test strategy is a **method of testing a completed system** to ensure **all parts work as intended**.

front_blocks.md: How is a system that is designed in modules tested?

back_blocks.md: Each module is tested **independently**, and testing is done again once all modules are **joined together**.

cards.front_md: How is a system that is designed in modules tested?
cards.back_md: Each module is tested **independently**, and testing is done again once all modules are **joined together**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Once changes have been made to a system, it does not need to be tested again.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Testing is **repeated** once all changes have been made.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Once changes have been made to a system, it does not need to be tested again.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Testing is **repeated** once all changes have been made.

front_blocks.md: Name the five things a test design covers.

back_blocks.md: A test design covers **data structures**, **file structures**, **input formats**, **output formats** and **validation routines**.

cards.front_md: Name the five things a test design covers.
cards.back_md: A test design covers **data structures**, **file structures**, **input formats**, **output formats** and **validation routines**.

front_blocks.md: Why are validation routines tested?

back_blocks.md: Validation routines are tested to check that the system **rejects unreasonable data** being inputted.

cards.front_md: Why are validation routines tested?
cards.back_md: Validation routines are tested to check that the system **rejects unreasonable data** being inputted.

front_blocks.md: What four things does a test plan include?

back_blocks.md: A test plan includes the **test data**, the **expected outcomes**, the **actual outcomes** and any **remedial action**.

cards.front_md: What four things does a test plan include?
cards.back_md: A test plan includes the **test data**, the **expected outcomes**, the **actual outcomes** and any **remedial action**.

front_blocks.md: Define **remedial action**.

back_blocks.md: Remedial action is the **steps taken to fix identified issues**.

cards.front_md: Define **remedial action**.
cards.back_md: Remedial action is the **steps taken to fix identified issues**.

front_blocks.md: Name the four categories of test data.

back_blocks.md: The four categories of test data are **normal**, **extreme**, **abnormal** and **live**.

cards.front_md: Name the four categories of test data.
cards.back_md: The four categories of test data are **normal**, **extreme**, **abnormal** and **live**.

front_blocks.md: Define **normal data**.

back_blocks.md: Normal data is data that **should be accepted** by the system and that has a **known outcome**.

cards.front_md: Define **normal data**.
cards.back_md: Normal data is data that **should be accepted** by the system and that has a **known outcome**.

front_blocks.md: Define **extreme data**.

back_blocks.md: Extreme data is data that is **on the limits of what is acceptable**.

cards.front_md: Define **extreme data**.
cards.back_md: Extreme data is data that is **on the limits of what is acceptable**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Extreme data should be rejected by the system.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Extreme data is **on the limits of what is acceptable**, so it is accepted. It is **abnormal data**, which is outside the limits of what is acceptable, that should be rejected.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Extreme data should be rejected by the system.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Extreme data is **on the limits of what is acceptable**, so it is accepted. It is **abnormal data**, which is outside the limits of what is acceptable, that should be rejected.

front_blocks.md: <u>**      **</u> data is data from the old system used on the new system.

back_blocks.md: **Live** data is data from the old system used on the new system.

cards.front_md: <u>**      **</u> data is data from the old system used on the new system.
cards.back_md: **Live** data is data from the old system used on the new system.

front_blocks.md: Why is live data useful when testing a new system?

back_blocks.md: Live data has **known outcomes**, so the results can be **compared** with the old system to ensure the new system works.

cards.front_md: Why is live data useful when testing a new system?
cards.back_md: Live data has **known outcomes**, so the results can be **compared** with the old system to ensure the new system works.

front_blocks.md: What is the purpose of the implementation stage?

back_blocks.md: The purpose of implementation is to **deploy the system to the production environment** and ensure all components work together in the **live setting**.

cards.front_md: What is the purpose of the implementation stage?
cards.back_md: The purpose of implementation is to **deploy the system to the production environment** and ensure all components work together in the **live setting**.

front_blocks.md: When does system implementation take place?

back_blocks.md: Implementation takes place **after a system has been fully tested** and is working correctly.

cards.front_md: When does system implementation take place?
cards.back_md: Implementation takes place **after a system has been fully tested** and is working correctly.

front_blocks.md: What are the two stages of system implementation?

back_blocks.md: The two stages are **transferring data from the old system to the new system** and the **system changeover**.

cards.front_md: What are the two stages of system implementation?
cards.back_md: The two stages are **transferring data from the old system to the new system** and the **system changeover**.

front_blocks.md: Define **changeover**.

back_blocks.md: A changeover is **moving from the old system to the new system**.

cards.front_md: Define **changeover**.
cards.back_md: A changeover is **moving from the old system to the new system**.

front_blocks.md: Name the four methods of changeover.

back_blocks.md: The four methods of changeover are **direct**, **parallel**, **pilot running** and **phased**.

cards.front_md: Name the four methods of changeover.
cards.back_md: The four methods of changeover are **direct**, **parallel**, **pilot running** and **phased**.

front_blocks.md: Define **direct changeover**.

back_blocks.md: In a direct changeover the **old system is replaced by the new system immediately**.

cards.front_md: Define **direct changeover**.
cards.back_md: In a direct changeover the **old system is replaced by the new system immediately**.

front_blocks.md: Define **parallel running**.

back_blocks.md: In parallel running **both the old and the new systems run simultaneously** for a period before the old system is phased out.

cards.front_md: Define **parallel running**.
cards.back_md: In parallel running **both the old and the new systems run simultaneously** for a period before the old system is phased out.

front_blocks.md: Which changeover method implements the new system in one branch of a company?

back_blocks.md: **Pilot running** implements the new system in a **small, controlled environment** before full-scale implementation.

cards.front_md: Which changeover method implements the new system in one branch of a company?
cards.back_md: **Pilot running** implements the new system in a **small, controlled environment** before full-scale implementation.

front_blocks.md: In <u>**      **</u> implementation the new system is introduced in stages, with each stage replacing a part of the old system.

back_blocks.md: In **phased** implementation the new system is introduced in stages, with each stage replacing a part of the old system.

cards.front_md: In <u>**      **</u> implementation the new system is introduced in stages, with each stage replacing a part of the old system.
cards.back_md: In **phased** implementation the new system is introduced in stages, with each stage replacing a part of the old system.

front_blocks.md: Give one advantage of a direct changeover.

back_blocks.md: A direct changeover gives **fast implementation** and is **cost-effective**, because only one system is in operation.

cards.front_md: Give one advantage of a direct changeover.
cards.back_md: A direct changeover gives **fast implementation** and is **cost-effective**, because only one system is in operation.

front_blocks.md: Give two disadvantages of a direct changeover.

back_blocks.md: A direct changeover has a **high risk of failure**, **no fallback**, **no backup of the system**, and users **cannot be trained** on the new system beforehand.

cards.front_md: Give two disadvantages of a direct changeover.
cards.back_md: A direct changeover has a **high risk of failure**, **no fallback**, **no backup of the system**, and users **cannot be trained** on the new system beforehand.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Parallel running is cheaper than a direct changeover.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Parallel running is **time-consuming and resource-intensive** because two systems run at once. A **direct** changeover is the cost-effective method.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Parallel running is cheaper than a direct changeover.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Parallel running is **time-consuming and resource-intensive** because two systems run at once. A **direct** changeover is the cost-effective method.

front_blocks.md: Give one advantage of parallel running.

back_blocks.md: Parallel running has a **lower risk** and allows **easy comparison** of the two systems.

cards.front_md: Give one advantage of parallel running.
cards.back_md: Parallel running has a **lower risk** and allows **easy comparison** of the two systems.

front_blocks.md: Give one disadvantage of pilot running.

back_blocks.md: Pilot running gives **slower implementation**, **potential inconsistencies**, **confusion** because two systems are in use, and **no backup** for the branch using the new system.

cards.front_md: Give one disadvantage of pilot running.
cards.back_md: Pilot running gives **slower implementation**, **potential inconsistencies**, **confusion** because two systems are in use, and **no backup** for the branch using the new system.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Phased implementation reduces risk and is easier to manage.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Phased implementation gives **reduced risk** and is **easier to manage**, but it **takes longer** and there may be **compatibility issues**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Phased implementation reduces risk and is easier to manage.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

Phased implementation gives **reduced risk** and is **easier to manage**, but it **takes longer** and there may be **compatibility issues**.

front_blocks.md: Define **technical documentation**.

back_blocks.md: Technical documentation is **detailed information on the system's inner workings and programming** for **developers and IT staff**.

cards.front_md: Define **technical documentation**.
cards.back_md: Technical documentation is **detailed information on the system's inner workings and programming** for **developers and IT staff**.

front_blocks.md: What three things does technical documentation allow the system to be?

back_blocks.md: Technical documentation enables the system to be **maintained**, **repaired** and **updated**.

cards.front_md: What three things does technical documentation allow the system to be?
cards.back_md: Technical documentation enables the system to be **maintained**, **repaired** and **updated**.

front_blocks.md: Define **user documentation**.

back_blocks.md: User documentation is **instructions and guidance for end-users on how to operate the system**.

cards.front_md: Define **user documentation**.
cards.back_md: User documentation is **instructions and guidance for end-users on how to operate the system**.

front_blocks.md: What does user documentation enable end-users to do?

back_blocks.md: User documentation enables end-users to **effectively use the system** and **overcome problems**.

cards.front_md: What does user documentation enable end-users to do?
cards.back_md: User documentation enables end-users to **effectively use the system** and **overcome problems**.

front_blocks.md: Name three items found in technical documentation but not in user documentation.

back_blocks.md: Items found only in technical documentation include the **program listing**, **program language**, **program flowcharts/algorithms**, **system flowcharts**, **file structures**, **list of variables**, **test runs** and **validation routines**.

cards.front_md: Name three items found in technical documentation but not in user documentation.
cards.back_md: Items found only in technical documentation include the **program listing**, **program language**, **program flowcharts/algorithms**, **system flowcharts**, **file structures**, **list of variables**, **test runs** and **validation routines**.

front_blocks.md: Name three items found in both technical and user documentation.

back_blocks.md: Both include the **purpose of the system**, its **limitations**, the **hardware and software requirements**, the **input format**, the **output format** and **sample runs**.

cards.front_md: Name three items found in both technical and user documentation.
cards.back_md: Both include the **purpose of the system**, its **limitations**, the **hardware and software requirements**, the **input format**, the **output format** and **sample runs**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A glossary of terms is part of technical documentation.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A **glossary of terms** is part of **user documentation**, along with frequently asked questions and a troubleshooting guide.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A glossary of terms is part of technical documentation.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

A **glossary of terms** is part of **user documentation**, along with frequently asked questions and a troubleshooting guide.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The limitations of a system appear in both technical and user documentation.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
**Limitations**, meaning the known constraints or issues with the system, appear in **both** types of documentation.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

The limitations of a system appear in both technical and user documentation.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

**Limitations**, meaning the known constraints or issues with the system, appear in **both** types of documentation.

front_blocks.md: Which two items in user documentation help a user solve common problems?

back_blocks.md: A **troubleshooting guide/helpline** and **frequently asked questions** help a user solve common problems.

cards.front_md: Which two items in user documentation help a user solve common problems?
cards.back_md: A **troubleshooting guide/helpline** and **frequently asked questions** help a user solve common problems.

front_blocks.md: Which type of documentation explains error messages and error handling?

back_blocks.md: **User documentation** explains **error messages** and **error handling**.

cards.front_md: Which type of documentation explains error messages and error handling?
cards.back_md: **User documentation** explains **error messages** and **error handling**.

back_blocks.md: User documentation explains **adding records** and **deleting or editing records**.

cards.front_md: Give two instructions about records that appear in user documentation.
cards.back_md: User documentation explains **adding records** and **deleting or editing records**.

front_blocks.md: What are system flowcharts used to show?

back_blocks.md: System flowcharts are **visual representations of the interactions between system components**.

cards.front_md: What are system flowcharts used to show?
cards.back_md: System flowcharts are **visual representations of the interactions between system components**.

front_blocks.md: What three things must you assess to evaluate a system?

back_blocks.md: You must assess the **efficiency**, the **ease of use** and the **appropriateness** of the solution.

cards.front_md: What three things must you assess to evaluate a system?
cards.back_md: You must assess the **efficiency**, the **ease of use** and the **appropriateness** of the solution.

front_blocks.md: What can you do once a system has been successfully evaluated?

back_blocks.md: You can **identify limitations** and **propose improvements**.

cards.front_md: What can you do once a system has been successfully evaluated?
cards.back_md: You can **identify limitations** and **propose improvements**.

front_blocks.md: A system's efficiency is evaluated in terms of which three things?

back_blocks.md: Efficiency is evaluated in terms of **resource usage**, **time** and **cost**.

cards.front_md: A system's efficiency is evaluated in terms of which three things?
cards.back_md: Efficiency is evaluated in terms of **resource usage**, **time** and **cost**.

front_blocks.md: Give one question you would ask when evaluating efficiency.

back_blocks.md: You would ask whether the system **operates quicker than the previous system**, whether it **reduces staff time**, or whether it **reduces staff costs**.

cards.front_md: Give one question you would ask when evaluating efficiency.
cards.back_md: You would ask whether the system **operates quicker than the previous system**, whether it **reduces staff time**, or whether it **reduces staff costs**.

front_blocks.md: Define **ease of use** in an evaluation.

back_blocks.md: Ease of use is **how user-friendly and accessible the solution is** for its intended audience.

cards.front_md: Define **ease of use** in an evaluation.
cards.back_md: Ease of use is **how user-friendly and accessible the solution is** for its intended audience.

front_blocks.md: Give one question you would ask when evaluating ease of use.

back_blocks.md: You would ask whether all users can **complete their tasks easily** and whether staff can **understand how to use the system with minimal training**.

cards.front_md: Give one question you would ask when evaluating ease of use.
cards.back_md: You would ask whether all users can **complete their tasks easily** and whether staff can **understand how to use the system with minimal training**.

front_blocks.md: How is the appropriateness of a solution evaluated?

back_blocks.md: Appropriateness is evaluated by **comparing the implemented solution with the original task requirements** and judging **how well it meets the intended purpose**.

cards.front_md: How is the appropriateness of a solution evaluated?
cards.back_md: Appropriateness is evaluated by **comparing the implemented solution with the original task requirements** and judging **how well it meets the intended purpose**.

User feedback forms part of the evaluation of a system.

User feedback forms part of the evaluation of a system.
cards.back_md:

Evaluating a system only means checking whether it works.

cards.front_md:

Evaluating a system only means checking whether it works.

Evaluation assesses the **efficiency**, **ease of use** and **appropriateness** of the solution, not just whether it functions.

front_blocks.md: Name two evaluation strategies.

back_blocks.md: Evaluation strategies include **comparing the final solution with the user requirements**, **identifying limitations**, **identifying further improvements**, **analysing feedback from users** and **comparing test results from the new system with the old system**.

front_blocks.md: What should be summarised when reporting the testing process in an evaluation?

back_blocks.md: The summary should cover the **test data**, the **expected outcomes** and the **actual outcomes**.
